item.title: Hunt exploitable vulnerabilities in your own app (Sponsor)
item.description: Don't have Mythos access? Chainguard Harness builds your app from source in an isolated environment, then lets Mythos 5.1 hunt through a live instance for exploitable vulnerabilities. Each finding is reproducible and delivered with a recommended fix.> Catch risks early: Find and patch exploitable vulnerabilities in your custom code and OSS before attackers do.> Refocus engineering: Reproducible findings focus team attention and resources on the most actionable issues that are based specifically on your code.> Avoid a massive bill: Skip building a custom test harness and burning cash on unoptimized tokens.Join the Chainguard Harness waitlist.

item.title: Announcing the Workload Conformance Working Group (4 minute read)
item.description: The Kubernetes community launched a Workload Conformance Working Group to write a shared specification and tests for how workloads behave at runtime. The group aims for a stable first specification within two to three release cycles and seeks input from operators and application maintainers.

item.title: Match monitoring depth to workload needs with Infrastructure Basic (4 minute read)
item.description: Datadog describes Infrastructure Basic, a lightweight tier that collects core host metrics and selected process status for lower-priority workloads. It uses the same Agent in basic mode and can run alongside Pro or Enterprise tiers in one organization.

item.title: Supabase Compute: run your agents inside your project (3 minute read)
item.description: Supabase launched Supabase Compute in private alpha to run agents, background jobs, and APIs directly alongside user data. The offering currently supports the us-west-2 region. Dreambase reported query latency dropped from 65 ms in another region to a median of 2.9 ms after moving a data agent to the new platform.

item.title: One Hub, 34 Clusters: Lessons From a GitOps Control Plane at Scale (5 minute read)
item.description: Nitish Mane describes an Argo CD hub that managed 34 clusters across 22 AWS accounts and one Oracle Cloud tenancy from a repository of 174 Helm charts. Per-cluster contracts, CI manifest diffs, and no-prune settings kept changes safe, and onboarding reportedly fell from 4 days to 1.7 hours.

item.title: How to Integrate Terraform with Backstage for Self-Service (17 minute read)
item.description: Mattias Fjellström explains how to connect Terraform with Backstage through the software catalog, software templates that open pull requests, and the Spacelift plugin. Backstage collects requests but does not run Terraform, so version control remains the source of truth.

item.title: 1M Durable Workflows per Second on Postgres (6 minute read)
item.description: DBOS scaled a benchmark of no-op durable workflows from 20,000 per second on one Postgres server to one million across 50 shards using PgDog. The main obstacle was a contention feedback loop that collapsed throughput when a shard slowed down. Advisory locks limited concurrent dequeuers and restored stable scaling.

item.title: Macro (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Macro is a unified workspace that combines email, chat, docs, tasks, agents, and CRM into a single interface with shared team memory. It links all objects, such as emails and tasks, via a bidirectional graph so AI agents and users can search across tools without switching contexts.

item.title: DeepTutor (GitHub Repo)
item.description: DeepTutor provides lifelong personalized tutoring with features like folder-based learning workspaces, daily practice, and persistent usage accounting. The open source platform includes over 100 CLI apps the tutor can run, supports OpenAI Codex OAuth for sign-in, and offers MCP Services stores on a per-account basis.

item.title: The AI observability race will be won on interoperability (5 minute read)
item.description: OpenTelemetry offers a common method to capture and describe AI behavior using shared conventions for conversations and messages. This standardization helps teams compare models, reduce duplicate integration work, and measure cost per outcome rather than just token counts.

item.title: The Pwn Request Reckoning: What Still Works Against GitHub Actions (9 minute read)
item.description: GitHub's upcoming platform changes in 2026 will make pull_request_target attacks harder, but gaps remain involving outdated checkout versions, script injection, and unprotected triggers like issue_comment. Pinning actions to old SHA values predating the July 2026 backport release bypasses the new checkout protections entirely. The default policy also does not apply to private repositories or workflow_run events.

item.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows generally available (3 minute read)
item.description: GitHub Agentic Workflows automates reasoning-based tasks like issue triage and CI failure analysis using coding agents inside GitHub Actions.

item.title: One pod, one node: The architecture behind serverless Kubernetes on AWS (8 minute read)
item.description: AWS Fargate for EKS routes pods with an admission webhook, provisions a dedicated environment per pod through its own scheduler, and attaches each pod to the customer VPC through a dedicated network interface.

item.title: Add RAG to your Elastic stack (Sponsor)
item.description: Your data is already in Elasticsearch — use Elastic Cloud to power Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). Skip the new database and add vector storage and LLM-powered search without changing your stack.Reuse your data layer: Store vector embeddings directly in Elasticsearch indices alongside your existing data — no separate vector database requiredWire up RAG end to end: Connect Elastic Cloud, LangChain, and Amazon Bedrock with a working Python pipeline from document ingestion to LLM queryAccess models through a unified API: Use Elasticsearch's Open Inference API to call Amazon Bedrock models for chat completion and text embeddingsFollow the step-by-step tutorial and start asking questions of your data today.Build a RAG pipeline on AWS >

item.title: Gheist: Attempted Scaled Abuse of Stolen GitHub Tokens Stumbles (9 minute read)
item.description: Gheist is an automated campaign that plants secret-dumping workflows in repositories using stolen GitHub tokens. It has targeted over 850 compromised accounts since September 15. GitHub's recent security controls blocked the attack in public repositories, but private and enterprise environments remain vulnerable.

item.title: What Took the Internet Offline in Q3 2026 (8 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare Radar recorded 49 Internet disruptions during the third quarter, including 19 government-directed shutdowns and 14 power outages. The incidents illustrate dependencies beyond network redundancy.

item.title: How to Build Golden Paths in Platform Engineering (19 minute read)
item.description: Spacelift defines a golden path as an opinionated, documented, self-service route for a common task. The guide lists five building blocks and four rollout phases, with a worked Postgres example on AWS built as an rds-postgres module using OpenTofu 1.10.3. Production gets Multi-AZ and deletion protection.

item.title: Why Kubernetes autoscalers keep fighting each other (and why the solution must be autonomous) (7 minute read)
item.description: Nikhil Kurup argues that HPA, VPA, KEDA, and Karpenter mutate the same workload fields from independent loops, producing four failure modes, including a VPA and HPA death spiral and GitOps drift ping-pong. He calls for a unified, predictive autoscaler with explainable decisions.

item.title: The Bridge to Agent-Scale Git Infrastructure (8 minute read)
item.description: GitHub is replacing repository-wide write serialization with per-reference quorums to overcome cross-region latency during its Azure migration. Internal tests showed 3–4x higher throughput for writes to different references, while an object-storage-backed design allows read capacity to scale independently.

item.title: How do you respond when your AI tooling and models fail? (Sponsor)
item.description: Engineers from incident.io and Skyscanner discuss what happens when AI tooling becomes a single point of failure, and what both teams are doing about it. Watch Now→

item.title: Agent-Reach (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Agent-Reach is an open source CLI tool that lets agents read and search platforms like Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, and Bilibili without API fees. It handles login-gated sites, video content, and Chinese platforms to provide structured data for AI agents.

item.title: OpenBot (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenBot is a local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates that runs Codex, Claude, Grok, and Gemini with dedicated workspaces and task queues. It provides a shared desktop channel, file transfers, and an embedded browser that agents can control. A development preview is available for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

item.title: Before you expand your GPU pool, measure the outcome (8 minute read)
item.description: Teams should define each workload's outcome and deadline before expanding a GPU pool. Teams can stagger flexible jobs, load test sustainable serving capacity, and track cost per verified outcome with OpenCost before adding GPUs.

item.title: Fixing Tool-Call Accuracy in vLLM (7 minute read)
item.description: vLLM 0.31 can achieve 100% tool-call schema accuracy for Kimi and DeepSeek models through constrained decoding, a technique that guarantees schema adherence during token generation. This fixes a reliability issue where vLLM 0.28 produced invalid tool calls 8% of the time, causing agentic workloads to build up nonsensical context.

item.title: The AI Software Factory Summit - SF 30% Off Ticket (Sponsor)
item.description: Explore advanced AI software use cases live in production showcased by Kelsey Hightower and leaders from NVIDIA, GitHub, and SpaceX this Nov 17–18 in SF. Discount code TLDR_30%Claim Your 30% Off Ticket

item.title: Scope Your Personal Access Tokens (6 minute read)
item.description: Supabase personal access tokens can be restricted to specific organizations, projects, permissions, and expiration dates for CI pipelines and other integrations.

item.title: PyTorch Conference 2026: Google and Meta Open-Source TorchTPU for Native PyTorch on TPUs (4 minute read)
item.description: Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google's TPUs, at PyTorch Conference North America 2026.

item.title: Observability patterns for AI agents on Amazon EKS (20 minute read)
item.description: AWS engineers compare two observability patterns for AI agents on Amazon EKS.

item.title: Get your AI agent through security review (Sponsor)
item.description: Security approval is the top blocker to shipping AI agents, cited by 42% of teams in Nylas's State of Agentic AI: H2 2026 survey. Nylas IAM makes the reviewer's question easy to answer. Each service and agent gets its own API key, limited by permission and by boundary, from one mailbox up to a whole organization. Nylas checks every request before it reaches the provider and logs every call, including the ones it refuses. A read-only agent can draft a reply but can't send it. IAM is included on every plan.See how Nylas IAM works

item.title: Expanding Claude availability and deployment choice on Google Cloud (2 minute read)
item.description: Google Cloud now offers an Anthropic-managed deployment option for Claude models alongside its Google-managed one. Both provide the same models on day zero at the same pricing. The Anthropic-managed option adds immediate access to Claude Platform features such as Managed Agents.

item.title: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available (1 minute read)
item.description: AWS has made Continuum for code vulnerabilities generally available. It builds a context graph of an AWS environment, tests findings for exploitability in a sandbox, and opens pull requests with patches. Teams start in Learn mode and can move to Enforce mode.

item.title: Broccoli2shell: Everything You Need To Know About The Critical Brotli Decoder Vulnerability (5 minute read)
item.description: CVE-2026-111497, also known as Broccoli2Shell, is a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decompression library that allows remote code execution. The flaw affects Node.js, Bun, and Envoy Proxy. Wiz data shows 91% of cloud environments have vulnerable resources. Organizations should apply security updates and rebuild affected workloads.

item.title: Detecting and mitigating ZDI-CAN-33367 and five other Linux flaws (8 minute read)
item.description: A working root exploit for Linux kernel bug ZDI-CAN-33367 is public before a CVE or fix is available. TuxCare reproduced the proof of concept for local privilege escalation on Ubuntu, Debian, and AlmaLinux. A separate patch for the flaw is reviewed but not merged, and none of the six disclosed bugs has a CVE ID yet.

item.title: Shard design doesn't start from your tables (7 minute read)
item.description: Neki "shard groups" let users co-locate related tables like customers and orders on the same physical cluster to keep joins and transactions local. Reference tables replicate lookup data to every shard, while global secondary indexes support queries that lack the shard key.

item.title: Origin Range Requests: Serving Large Files Without Range-Request Tuning (9 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare rebuilt range-request caching in Pingora to coordinate partial downloads across cached data and in-flight origin fetches. The redesign roughly halved R2's p99 time to first byte and eliminated customer-managed range sizes, while a follow-up improvement reduced tiered-cache traffic for R2 and similar workloads by about 6%.

item.title: How the AWS Nitro System Delivers Confidential Computing (Sponsor)
item.description: Protecting workloads from cloud operator access shouldn't require work on your part. The AWS Nitro System provides strong isolation — monitoring, protecting, and verifying instance hardware and firmware. There is no mechanism for any person, including AWS's most privileged admins, to access instance memory. Learn more.

item.title: Coolify (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Coolify is an open-source, self-hostable PaaS alternative to Vercel, Heroku, and Netlify. It allows users to deploy static sites, databases, and full-stack applications on their own servers. The tool offers more than 360 one-click services and automatic HTTPS certificates.

item.title: QuestDB 10.1: Fresher Data, Less I/O, and More Analysis in SQL (12 minute read)
item.description: QuestDB 10.1 adds optional merge-append partitions that reduce rewriting when late data arrives, with background compaction reclaiming obsolete rows. On QuestDB's public demo, enabling the feature reduced rows written per ingested row from about 440 to 8. The release also adds exact percentiles and SQL subsampling.

item.title: Scale isn't one number: three ways a Kubernetes control plane runs out of room (8 minute read)
item.description: Kubernetes control planes run out of room in three independent ways: node count, object churn, and resident state. Joe Betz of Google describes four seams, including storage routing and cache residency, and a recipe ladder built from stock upstream components. Some seams still have upstream gaps.

item.title: Railway Preliminary Report: Oct 21st Security Incident (7 minute read)
item.description: Railway disclosed a security incident where an attacker accessed internal systems from October 20 to 22 to target AI provider API keys. Environment variables for approximately 100,000 workspaces, or 1.85% of the total, were potentially compromised. Railway revoked credentials with partner vendors and accelerated a rollout of single-tenant builder infrastructure.

item.description: Grafana Labs proposes applying SLOs and error budgets to AI agent behavior, such as a 95% target for fulfilled conversations over 30 days.

item.title: Prompt Caching is GA on DigitalOcean Serverless Inference: Up to 90% Off the Context Your Agents Resend (6 minute read)
item.description: Prompt caching is now generally available on DigitalOcean Serverless Inference.

item.title: Confidential Computing Built into EC2 Instances (Sponsor)
item.description: Every security review asks: what can the cloud provider access? The AWS Nitro System was built with no operator access, and no code changes required:🚫 No operator access by design: No system or person can log in to Nitro hosts, read instance memory, or access customer data on encrypted EBS volumes.📋 Authenticated, audited APIs only: Even AWS's most privileged operators are limited to authorized, audited APIs, none of which can access customer data.⚡ Near bare-metal performance: The Nitro Hypervisor performs like bare metal for most workloads, so isolation doesn't cost throughput.Learn how the AWS Nitro System delivers confidential computing →

item.title: Introducing Harness AI Budgets (5 minute read)
item.description: Harness AI Budgets turns AI cost policies into enforced weekly spending limits scoped to a team, developer, model, or project. Access pauses at 100% until the weekly reset or an approved increase. In Harness' internal test, weekly AI spend per developer fell about 37%.

item.title: Critical PHP RCE Vulnerabilities: Patch Now (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) (5 minute read)
item.description: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, were publicly disclosed on October 21. Proof-of-concept exploit code is available, and the flaws affect every PHP version from PHP 5 onward. DigitalOcean is automatically patching WordPress instances on its Cloudways managed product, but customers running PHP on Droplets or other unmanaged services must update to PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, or 8.5.12 immediately. There are no patches for PHP 8.1 or earlier.

item.title: ObservabilityCON 2026: A guide to all the announcements from Grafana Labs (10 minute read)
item.description: Grafana Labs announced Grafana Cloud updates covering AI operations, cost controls, and full-stack context. Assistant Watchers reached general availability, Adaptive Telemetry customers report cutting spend 30% to 50% on average, and the Grafana Marketplace launched with more than 30 plugins.

item.title: Scaling GitOps With Release Promotion (4 minute read)
item.description: Jesse Suen of Akuity describes a fleet of over 200 clusters where every merge synced everywhere with no gate. He argues sync tools do not handle release tracking or promotion decisions and recommends staged promotion that rolls out in waves and halts on failed checks.

item.title: I Don't Trust ON DELETE CASCADE (6 minute read)
item.description: Large cascading deletes can turn a routine schema migration into an outage by holding locks while new queries queue behind the waiting migration. Soft deletes followed by bounded background cleanup keep transactions smaller, with additional pitfalls around unindexed foreign keys and logical replication.

item.title: Presentation: AI is an Amplifier: Scale High Performance, Not Dysfunction (33 minute read)
item.description: Nathen Harvey of Google Cloud's DORA team presents 2025 survey findings from nearly 5,000 respondents, about 90% of whom use AI professionally. He argues AI amplifies existing organizational strengths and dysfunctions, and introduces the DORA AI Capabilities Model.

item.title: JEV helps your agent decide what to do next. Bluehost gives it somewhere to run 24/7. (Sponsor)
item.description: Your agent shouldn't depend on your laptop staying open. Run it on an always-on VPS with a 99.99% uptime guarantee, so it keeps working after you log offGet started

item.title: Claude-How-To (GitHub Repo)
item.description: This MIT-licensed guide teaches users how to use Claude Code through 10 modules covering slash commands, hooks, skills, and MCP servers. Users can copy templates directly into projects or follow a self-assessment quiz to get a personalized roadmap. The current version, v2.1.302, is compatible with Claude Code 2.1+ and includes copy-paste templates for models including Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5.

item.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Lockfiles in Public Preview (2 minute read)
item.description: GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles pin actions and their transitive dependencies to reviewed commits while preserving readable tags in workflow files. The public preview includes a GitHub CLI extension to generate lockfiles, Dependabot integration to update them, and policies that require workflows to use them.

item.title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know (4 minute read)
item.description: Private keys for eight widely trusted eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised on October 19, allowing attackers to forge certificates for any domain. Cloudflare has patched its CDN, Zero Trust, and Tunnel products. Customers must update the Cloudflare One Client and 1.1.1.1 app to specific versions to remain protected.

item.title: Before you evaluate an AI SRE, give your existing agent context (6 minute read)
item.description: Engineers at Radar tested whether adding context to coding agents improves Kubernetes diagnostics. When running 50 fault scenarios, agents with context reached a correct diagnosis within two minutes on 86% of faults, compared to 60% for agents using a standard shell. Accuracy improved only slightly with context, but the time savings were significant. The test used Claude Code and Microsoft's SREGym benchmark on a live Amazon EKS cluster.

item.title: AI infrastructure on tap with the Pulumi AICR provider (3 minute read)
item.description: Pulumi has released the NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) provider to help developers deploy self-hosted AI infrastructure.

item.title: GitHub Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0 Targets Reliability at Scale (3 minute read)
item.description: GitHub released Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0, which sends smaller patch requests and moves runner status aggregation into metrics to reduce Kubernetes API updates.

item.title: Stack Overflow for Agents triples signups with ChatGPT plugin (3 minute read)
item.description: Stack Overflow built Stack Overflow for Agents in a few weeks with two engineers using Codex. A ChatGPT plugin reportedly tripled overnight registrations, and Codex cut enterprise connector build time from 3 to 6 weeks to 4 days.

item.title: Introducing Amazon ECS Gateway: A fully-managed ingress solution for ECS services (4 minute read)
item.description: Amazon ECS Gateway is a resource that simplifies ingress networking for containerized workloads by automatically provisioning load balancers and certificates. It allows up to 25 services to share a single Application Load Balancer to optimize infrastructure costs. Amazon ECS Gateway is available now in all commercial AWS Regions at no additional charge, though users pay for the underlying resources provisioned in their accounts.

item.title: Introducing tsrs: a Port of TypeScript to Rust (5 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare and VoidZero are collaborating on tsrs, a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler. Early benchmarks show tsrs is up to 8x faster and uses roughly 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0. The team is working with the TypeScript team to ensure the port remains compatible with the official language design. Rust allows the compiler to run in WebAssembly, which enables development environments to run in browsers or on embedded devices.

item.title: Redesigning Source Control at Anthropic (15 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic replaced Git for its monorepo with Scion, a centralized source control system designed for tens of millions of daily CI checkouts. Content-addressed storage, server-side repository operations, and tiered caches reduced its source-control CPU and memory footprint 200× compared with its previous Git mirroring infrastructure.

item.title: AI agents vs. Kubernetes: where each belongs in the control loop (6 minute read)
item.description: Kubernetes operators suit deterministic reconciliation, while AI agents suit goals with unclear paths, according to a CNCF-sponsored piece. Use an observe, diagnose, propose, approve, reconcile, and verify loop, with autonomy phased from read-only investigation to approved low-risk changes.

item.title: SIMD and Go (20 minute read)
item.description: Go's experimental SIMD packages expose vector instructions that process multiple values in one operation without handwritten assembly. Examples cover vector registers, loads, arithmetic, and compiler behavior using Go 1.27's experimental SIMD support on amd64.

item.title: What it actually takes to build an AI SRE (Sponsor)
item.description: Two years, hundreds of prompts, one adversarial agent. Here's what it really took us to build incident.io Investigations, and why the prototype is a trap. Read More →

item.title: Headroom (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Headroom compresses tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM. Benchmarks show the compression results in 20% fewer tokens for coding agents and 60-95% fewer tokens for JSON. The tool runs locally to ensure no prompt or file content is sent externally.

item.title: vLLM (GitHub Repo)
item.description: vLLM is a library for LLM inference and serving that originated in the Sky Computing Lab at UC Berkeley. The open-source project now has over 2,000 contributors and supports more than 200 model architectures on Hugging Face.

item.title: Cutting Our Inference Bill by 68% Through Optimization (15 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare reduced its AI code reviewer's average cost from $2.43 to $0.77 through shared prompt-cache prefixes, fewer redundant tool calls, and model and reasoning-effort changes. Median review time fell from 4 minutes 9 seconds to 1 minute 32 seconds, while quality checks exposed trade-offs where cheaper configurations missed important findings.

item.title: Inside Prometheus: Meta's Journey to a Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster (13 minute read)
item.description: Meta is building Prometheus, a gigawatt-scale supercluster in New Albany, Ohio, that will eventually comprise roughly 1 million GPUs. The first phase of the project has already trained the company's Muse foundational models. Meta achieved over 85% goodput for pre-training runs and reduced interruption rates by 99% from their peak. The cluster currently deploys NVIDIA GB200 and GB300 platforms, with plans to integrate the upcoming Vera Rubin NVL72 next.

item.description: Itaú is applying its AI-first strategy using OpenAI models, including the ia.i assistant that reached about 300,000 customers in its first phase.
